title: I made a Warcraft III-style hero RPG with Claude: plain JS, no engine, every sprite and note generated in code (about 2 hours of content, free in your browser)
author: real_person321
selftext:
Play: [https://dafioram.github.io/embervale/](https://dafioram.github.io/embervale/)

Source (MIT): [https://github.com/dafioram/embervale](https://github.com/dafioram/embervale)



Embervale is a small-party action RPG in the spirit of WC3's Rexxar campaign. You control three heroes (a warden tank, a shaman healer and an archer) through Act I, which takes about an hour, plus a 10-floor post-game dungeon that takes about another. It has 6 bosses with telegraphed attacks, quests, shops, gear that shows on your heroes, and music and weather for each zone.



The interesting part for this sub is that there are no asset files at all. Every character, tree and spell effect is drawn with canvas code, and every song and sound effect is synthesized with Web Audio. So the AI wasn't generating images or audio. It was writing the code that draws and plays them.



How I worked:

\- I played it constantly and kept a running list of changes, then had them built in batches rather than one-offs. That kept things from drifting.

\- I asked for mockups before committing to big changes: zone atmosphere, music options, art direction.

\- I tried a pre-rendered look and a low-poly look side by side before settling on flat vector.

\- I gave specific feedback from playtesting, like "fewer butterflies in Whisperwood" or "enemies keep chasing the hero I pulled back, make them fight the closest one".

\- The AI ran its own tests between batches: a bot that plays through all of Act I, screenshots of every zone, and frame-time measurements.



What went wrong and got fixed:

\- The first atmosphere pass ran smoothly in Chrome but crawled in Firefox on my old 4th-gen i5. Profiling showed per-frame canvas filters and tree sway were the problem. Moving to CSS blend layers and cached sprites made it smooth with no visible loss.

\- Some popups opened behind the title screen, and waypoints were placed oddly (one right next to town). Small things, but only playtesting caught them.



Happy to answer questions about the workflow. Feedback on the game itself is very welcome, especially on difficulty and anything confusing.
